To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-6 can signal via a soluble IL-6 receptor and that this trans-signaling is important for pro-inflammatory activities of the IL-6.
IL-6 has anti-inflammatory and regenerative functions and that IL-6 signaling is mediated by two different receptor complexes.
IL-6 has two different signaling pathways, one of which is pro-inflammatory, the other one is regenerative and anti-inflammatory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biology of interleukin-6.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of cytokine action.
the biology of cytokines, which are involved in the regulation of immunity and inflammation, in particular with the role of IL-6 in these processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-6 is a cytokine, which has both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory activities.
IL-6 is a cytokine that can be beneficial or detrimental to the organism depending on its mode of action.
IL-6 is a cytokine which has many functions in the body.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the blockade of IL-6 trans-signalization may be a promising strategy for the therapy of chronic inflammatory diseases, whereas the blockade of the IL-6/sIL-6R complex may have adverse effects.
the blockade of IL-6 trans-signalizing activities may have beneficial effects in diseases, which are associated with an inflammatory reaction.
IL-6 is an important cytokine, which has to be carefully balanced in order to maintain homeostasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

IL-6 blockade with antibodies directed against the IL-6 itself or the soluble IL-6R will be effective only in the treatment of IL-6 dependent autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, but not in the treatment of cancers, where classic IL-6 receptor signaling is required.
the blockade of IL-6 transsignaling is more efficient than the blockade of IL6 itself.
the IL-6 receptor is a major determinant of biological activity and that the soluble form of the receptor is an essential mediator of pro-inflammatory IL-6 activities in vivo.
